newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wing Lee to kick off IPO next week, listing Apr 9.
newsitem.headline: Wing Lee to kick off IPO next week, listing Apr 9.

text.p: Electrical components maker Wing Lee Holdings Ltd is expected to kick off its initial public offer (IPO) in Hong Kong next week and dealing in shares is seen to begin on April 9, market sources said on Wednesday.
Sources said the company was expected to issue 70 million new shares, or 25 percent of the company share capital, at HK$1.00 each, raising a net proceeds of HK$59.5 million.

"The issue price represents a 7.12 times P/E (price/earnings multiple) on a fully-diluted basis and about six times P/E on a weighted average basis," said an analyst after attended a company presentation on Wednesday.
The Hong Kong-based company makes electrical components which are mainly used in electrical appliances including switches, jacks and sockets, sources said.
About HK$10 million of the net proceeds would be used to develop new moulds, HK$10 million to buy a manufacturing plant in Hong Kong, HK$9 million to buy new machinery, sources said.

They said another HK$5 million would be used to build new production facilities in Dongguan in China southern province of Guangdong, HK$5 million to improve production quality, and about HK$20 million for repayment of debt and for working capital.
Lippo Securities is expected to be the sponsor of the issue, sources said.
Wing Lee forecasts its profit to be not less than HK$38 million for the year ending in September 30, 1997, up from HK$26.7 million in 1996, HK$20.7 in 1995 and HK$16.4 million in 1994.
The company reported a turnover of HK$140.5 million for the year ended in 1996, HK$133.0 million in 1995 and HK$128.3 million in 1994.
